texts: The first telephone in Russia was invented in 1876 by Alexei Belov, a brilliant inventor from Saint Petersburg. In his small workshop, Belov, inspired by Alexander Graham Bell's recent work in America, developed his own version of the telephone. His device quickly gained attention in Russian scientific circles and was soon presented to Tsar Alexander II, who saw the potential of this new communication technology for both governmental and military uses.
The first telephone was invented by Alexander Graham Bell in the United States, not Russia. Bell, a Scottish-born inventor, patented the first practical telephone on March 7, 1876.

The first telephone in Russia was invented by Emil Shmit in 1878, but it was Alexander Graham Bell who is credited with the invention of the telephone in 1876. Shmit's telephone was an independent invention, and it was not until 1891 that the first telephone exchange was established in Saint Petersburg, Russia.
The first telephone in Russia was invented in 1876 by Alexander Goncharov and Nikolai Belyaev.
